key_insight: A quasi-square-wave spanwise wall oscillation exposes a phase-dependent switch in the self-sustaining process: Reversal Phases let streaks regenerate, while Displacement Phases suppress them through Stokes-strain-driven vorticity diversion.
engineering_relevance: By redistributing the actuation timing rather than increasing actuation strength, the waveform improves gross drag reduction by 2.5 percentage points over the best sinusoidal baseline and clarifies how to design more effective wall-oscillation control.
method: Direct Numerical Simulation of turbulent channel flow at Re_tau ≈ 200 with spanwise wall actuation
Quasi-square-wave forcing split into Reversal and Displacement Phases for phase-resolved analysis
Stochastic enstrophy-budget analysis to verify the mechanism at the governing-equation level
evidence_signal: The abstract reports phase-resolved DNS and enstrophy-budget results showing that Stokes strain and mean-shear production compete for a shared vorticity reservoir, yielding a 2.5-point gross drag-reduction gain over the optimal sinusoidal case.
watch_item: The study is at moderate Reynolds number in DNS, so transferability to higher-Re flows and practical actuators may depend on actuator bandwidth and the ability to realize sharp waveform switching.
paper_title: Duty-cycle modulation of the self-sustaining process by spanwise wall oscillation
